title: Candidate verification API: how to verify job applicants
summary: How to verify job applicants with an API: send their details and résumé claims, and Sixtyfour researches them and returns each answer with its sources.
body_markdown:
A candidate verification API takes the details a job applicant gives you, such as their name, email address, phone number, LinkedIn URL and résumé claims, and returns a structured assessment. It says whether those details point to one real person, whether each employment and education claim is supported, contradicted or not found, and which sources each answer rests on. The assessment is evidence for a person on your team to review, and the decision stays with them.


Yes. Sixtyfour's People Intelligence endpoint takes what you know about an applicant and the fields you define, researches sources across the web and returns those fields with the pages it read. Define a field that lists each résumé claim with a status of supported, contradicted or not found, a sentence of evidence and a source URL, and the answer comes back in that shape, with every status one of the three you listed. Its Reverse Lookup endpoint shows who an email address or phone number resolves to.


Send each one to a reverse lookup, which returns the name, employer and profile it resolves to, and compare them with the application. With Sixtyfour's Reverse Lookup, a single request takes one email or one phone number, a lookup that finds nothing is free, and missing values come back as empty strings. Treat a lookup with no record as neutral, and send a different name to a person rather than reading it as fraud.


A contradicted claim has a source that says something incompatible with it, such as an announcement that dates a hire two years after the résumé does. A claim that is not found has no source either way, which is common for people with little public footprint and says nothing about whether the claim is true. Keep the two as separate statuses, and send only contradictions to review as a reason.


No. Names differ between sources for ordinary reasons, such as marriage, transliteration, a nickname or an old shared email address, and a single reverse lookup reflects the record it found. Show the difference to a reviewer with its source, and count it as a reason for review only when other evidence points the same way.


Pass an HTTPS webhook_url when you start the research, and Sixtyfour posts a delivery to it when the results are ready. A job that fails or is cancelled sends no delivery, so keep the job ID and poll it as a fallback. To start checks from your own system, send applicant rows to a workflow whose first block is a webhook block.


As of November 2026, People Intelligence costs 20 credits per applicant at the medium tier and 1 at low, with high at 40 on request. A reverse email match costs 0.5 credits and a reverse phone match 3, and a lookup that finds nothing is free. Polling a job and reading its results cost nothing, and a single research call that fails is free, though steps it completed stay charged.
